type: prospective power curve over the number of measurements
the_number: about 1,600 measured cell-by-pair combinations for 80 percent power

no_subsampling_bias.reading: the point estimate is stable across a thirty-two-fold range of measurement counts, so subsampling changes precision rather than the target

in_practice: at about 125 cell lines per drug pair, 1,600 keys is roughly thirteen drug pairs measured across all cells, a real screening campaign rather than a small exercise
why_this_matters: the promotion criterion requires cross-dataset replication, and this is the first estimate of what that replication would cost

an_unchecked_hypothesis.idea: if the three arenas used for cross-dataset attempts had far fewer than 1,600 usable combinations in the both-unseen regime, their failure was the expected outcome on power grounds alone
an_unchecked_hypothesis.status: not checked; needs the per-arena key counts
an_unchecked_hypothesis.value: it would turn the resource-limitation statement into a checkable arithmetic claim

limits: Subsampling draws from the existing evaluation pool, whose composition may differ from newly measured combinations.
The 80 percent and 0.05 conventions are conventions, not requirements.
next_gate: retrieve the actual key counts of the three cross-dataset arenas and test whether they fall short of 1,600
